note: The cost-of-margin curve, RESTORED 27 Aug 2026 on the corrected boundary using DERIVED targets. The previous version of this study was inert -- all sixteen margin points and both rescue points returned 'nothing above target', zero watts, zero blocks, because it asked for absolute 93-99 C while --spreading had dropped the die to 73-81 C. The handbook claim was withdrawn for want of any backing (catalogue_naming_and_margin_defects.json). It is now measured again.
the_fix: examples/mr_comparison.py gained --mr-target-offset-K: the target is derived from THIS POINT's measured unaided peak rather than stated as an absolute temperature. The reference arm is array_idle -- the same stack with the laser off -- and NOT the control: the control is a different stack, cooler by the passive term (7.4 K at d=0.80), so offsetting from it re-creates the same defect one layer down. That error was made and caught by smoke test before the batch ran.

RESULT_1_the_relation_holds_and_is_now_m.claim: The cost of a rescue rises steeply and nonlinearly with the margin demanded. Measured: ~24x more heat removed for 12 K of margin than for 1 K, and the consistency across three quite different configurations is the striking part.
RESULT_1_the_relation_holds_and_is_now_m.note_on_the_old_number: The superseded claim said 30-160x over 'a few kelvin' at densities of 1.10-1.15 W/mm^2, which do not exist on this boundary. The new measurement is over 1-12 K at 0.80-0.85 W/mm^2. Same SHAPE, different axis -- the numbers are not comparable and the old ones stay withdrawn.

RESULT_2_the_knee_is_the_plateau_being_e.what: Up to 2 K of margin the planner hits the target exactly using ONE block. From 3 K it can no longer hold the target -- achieved lags demanded -- and the engaged-block count explodes: 1 -> 3 -> 6 -> 12 -> 32 across 2/3/5/8/12 K.
RESULT_2_the_knee_is_the_plateau_being_e.why: Past the runner-up, cooling the peak means cooling everything between the target and the peak, which on this die is the plateau. It is the same overshoot the tile-pitch and die-average studies found: a targeted plan can only pull the peak down to the runner-up's level.

RESULT_3_this_OVERTURNS_the_uncomfortabl.the_old_claim: 'On a liquid-class sink at the same density the die holds 93.6 C unaided and MR engages ZERO blocks. Better conventional cooling did not make MR more valuable -- it made it irrelevant.'
RESULT_3_this_OVERTURNS_the_uncomfortabl.what_the_measurement_says_now: With a target derived from where the die actually sits, the liquid arm behaves ESSENTIALLY IDENTICALLY to the air arms: 25.1x cost rise against 24.0x and 23.9x, the same block-count explosion, the same knee. The cost-of-margin relation is a property of the die's TEMPERATURE DISTRIBUTION, not of the cooling class.
RESULT_3_this_OVERTURNS_the_uncomfortabl.the_honest_reconciliation: Both statements are true and they answer different questions. If the requirement is an ABSOLUTE temperature the die already meets, MR is irrelevant -- that is a real deployment consideration and it is unchanged. But it is a statement about the REQUIREMENT, not about MR or about liquid cooling. Ask instead what a given margin below the part's own operating point costs, and air and liquid are indistinguishable. The old framing attributed to the cooling class what belonged to the choice of target.
RESULT_3_this_OVERTURNS_the_uncomfortabl.so_what_stays_withdrawn: The 93.6 C figure and the 'MR is irrelevant under better cooling' conclusion. The mechanism -- that a target inside the plateau makes cooling anything mean cooling everything -- stands, and is now measured on all three configurations.
